#Background
This is for the Little Cayman Transplant. Corals were collected from 10 m and 40 m, cut in half, and then cross-transplanted. I have initial samples (T0) and final samples after 6 months on the reefs (TF). The experiment was done at Martha's Finyard and at Coral City. I have coral tissue and coral mucus samples from each coral. I also have environmental water samples from a variety of reefs around Little Cayman (T0) and from the experimental sites (T0 and TF). Sequencing was done in 5 libraries, one of which used MiSeq i100 (the rest were MiSeq). I will run learnError and dada2 separately for each sample type and library ID combination, resulting in 6 streams. Because MiSeq i100 results in a much higher number of reads per sample, these samples will be rarified. 

#General set up
```{r setup, include=FALSE}
setwd("~/Documents/WHOI/Projects/LittleCaymanTransplant_Analyses")
```


```{r}
library("dada2")
packageVersion("dada2") #need at least 1.37 for MiSeq i100

library(dplyr)
library(data.table)

```

#Set up learnError groups

```{r}
meta <- read.csv("Meta_Data.csv", header = TRUE)
dim(meta)

#Make data frames for each error rate group
unique_runs <- sort(unique(meta$Learn_error_number))

meta_1run <- meta[which(meta$Learn_error_number==unique_runs[1]),]
nrow(meta_1run)#57 --> Coral tissue, R2 

meta_2run <- meta[which(meta$Learn_error_number==unique_runs[2]),]
nrow(meta_2run) #26 --> Water, T2

meta_3run <- meta[which(meta$Learn_error_number==unique_runs[3]),]
nrow(meta_3run) #65 --> Coral tissue, V2

meta_4run <- meta[which(meta$Learn_error_number==unique_runs[4]),]
nrow(meta_4run) #98 --> Mucus, Y2

meta_5run <- meta[which(meta$Learn_error_number==unique_runs[5]),]
nrow(meta_5run) #21 --> Water, Y2

meta_6run <- meta[which(meta$Learn_error_number==unique_runs[6]),]
nrow(meta_6run) #15 --> Mucus, Z2

#make sure I have all my samples covered:
nrow(meta_1run) + nrow(meta_2run) + nrow(meta_3run) + nrow(meta_4run) + nrow(meta_5run) + nrow(meta_6run) 
#282, so I'm good!

```

Now we read in the names of the fastq files, and perform some string manipulation to get matched lists of the forward and reverse fastq files.

```{r}
# 1. List files
# Forward and reverse fastq filenames have format: SAMPLENAME_R1_001.fastq and SAMPLENAME_R2_001.fastq
fnFs <- sort(list.files(path, pattern="_R1_001.fastq", full.names = TRUE))
fnRs <- sort(list.files(path, pattern="_R2_001.fastq", full.names = TRUE))

# 2. Extract File_Name_Header from each file
  # Adjust this to match how your File_Name_Header appears in the filename
  # This assumes filenames like "Water_F_2_ACGCTACT-TAGCGAGT_L001_R1_001.fastq"
file_headers_F <- sapply(fnFs, function(x) {
  sub("L001_R1_001.fastq.gz$", "", basename(x))
}, USE.NAMES = FALSE)


# 3. Match to metadata
# Your metadata should be a data frame with File_Name_Header and Unique_ID as columns
# Match file headers to metadata
matched_df <- meta[match(file_headers_F, meta$File_Name_Header), ]


# 4. Confirm everything aligns
# Make sure all matched
stopifnot(all(!is.na(matched_df$Unique_ID)))
    #Error: all(!is.na(matched_df$Unique_ID)) is not TRUE

# 5. if there are unmatched names, find the unmatched names
# unmatched <- setdiff(file_headers_F, meta$File_Name_Header)
# if (length(unmatched) > 0) {
#   warning("Some file headers are not found in metadata:\n", paste(unmatched, collapse = "\n"))
# }


sample.names <- matched_df$Unique_ID
names(fnFs) <- sample.names
names(fnRs) <- sample.names

#Save
write.csv(sample.names, file = "sample_names.csv")
```
sample.names <- read.csv("sample_names.csv")



#Inspect read quality profiles

We start by visualizing the quality profiles of the forward reads. 
Going to look at the profiles for each learnError group
```{r}
# Coral tissue, R2
plotQualityProfile(fnFs[16:17])
    # not a strong drop off, I'd cut off 10

# Water, T2
plotQualityProfile(fnFs[123:124])
    # not a strong drop off, I'd cut off 10

# Coral tissue, V2
plotQualityProfile(fnFs[26:27])
    # not a strong drop off, I'd cut off 10

# Mucus, Y2
plotQualityProfile(fnFs[213:214])
    # not a strong drop off, I'd cut off 10

# Water, Y2
plotQualityProfile(fnFs[267:268])
    # not a strong drop off, I'd cut off 10

# Mucus, Z2
plotQualityProfile(fnFs[146:147])
    # no drop off, bc MiSeq i100

```
Decision: Cut of 10 based on forward reads at position 240. 


Now we visualize the quality profile of the reverse reads:
```{r}
# Coral tissue, R2
plotQualityProfile(fnRs[16:17])
    # Cut off ~50

# Water, T2
plotQualityProfile(fnRs[123:124])
    # Cut off ~25

# Coral tissue, V2
plotQualityProfile(fnRs[26:27])
    # Cut off ~50

# Mucus, Y2
plotQualityProfile(fnRs[213:214])
    # Cut off ~50

# Water, Y2
plotQualityProfile(fnRs[267:268])
    # Cut off ~30

# Mucus, Z2
plotQualityProfile(fnRs[146:147])
    # no drop off, bc MiSeq i100
```
Decision: Cut of 50 based on forward reads at position 200.



#Filter and trim

Assign the filenames for the filtered fastq.gz files.
```{r}
# Place filtered files in filtered/ subdirectory
filtFs <- file.path(path, "filtered", paste0(meta$File_Name_Header, "_F_filt.fastq.gz"))
filtRs <- file.path(path, "filtered", paste0(meta$File_Name_Header, "_R_filt.fastq.gz"))
names(filtFs) <- sample.names
names(filtRs) <- sample.names
```



```{r}
out <- filterAndTrim(fnFs, filtFs, fnRs, filtRs, truncLen=c(240,200),
              maxN=0, maxEE=c(2,2), truncQ=2, rm.phix=TRUE,
              compress=TRUE, multithread=TRUE)

#Save
save(out, file="/Users/jeannebloomberg/Documents/WHOI/Projects/Little_Cayman_Transplant_Analyses/out_filterAndTrim.RData")
```
load("/Users/jeannebloomberg/Documents/WHOI/Projects/Little_Cayman_Transplant_Analyses/out_filterAndTrim.RData")



# Learn the Error Rates
#### Forwards
Learn errors (F) for each sequencing run
```{r}
# Coral tissue, R2 (57 samples) 
filtFs_1run <- filtFs[meta_1run$Unique_ID]
errF_1run <- learnErrors(filtFs_1run, multithread = TRUE)

# Water, T2 (26 samples)
filtFs_2run <- filtFs[meta_2run$Unique_ID]
errF_2run <- learnErrors(filtFs_2run, multithread = TRUE)

# Coral tissue, V2 (65 samples)
filtFs_3run <- filtFs[meta_3run$Unique_ID]
errF_3run <- learnErrors(filtFs_3run, multithread = TRUE)

# Mucus, Y2 (98 samples)
filtFs_4run <- filtFs[meta_4run$Unique_ID]
errF_4run <- learnErrors(filtFs_4run, multithread = TRUE)

# Water, Y2 (21 samples)
filtFs_5run <- filtFs[meta_5run$Unique_ID]
errF_5run <- learnErrors(filtFs_5run, multithread = TRUE)

# Mucus, Z2 (15)
# Need to do this one differently, because it is MiSeq i100 that uses binned quality scores. See notes on WHOI/Projects/EEID-PREDICT-Shallowdada2_Water_Prelim.Rmd
filtFs_6run <- filtFs[meta_6run$Unique_ID]
binnedQs <- c(2, 12, 24, 38)
binnedQualErrfun <- makeBinnedQualErrfun(binnedQs)
errF_6run <-learnErrors(filtFs_6run, errorEstimationFunction=binnedQualErrfun, multi=TRUE)


#Save
save(errF_1run, file = "errF_1run.RData")
save(errF_2run, file = "errF_2run.RData")
save(errF_3run, file = "errF_3run.RData")
save(errF_4run, file = "errF_4run.RData")
save(errF_5run, file = "errF_5run.RData")
save(errF_6run, file = "errF_6run.RData")
```




#### Reverses
Learn errors (F) for each sequencing run
```{r}
# Coral tissue, R2 (57 samples) 
filtRs_1run <- filtRs[meta_1run$Unique_ID]
errR_1run <- learnErrors(filtRs_1run, multithread = TRUE)

# Water, T2 (26 samples)
filtRs_2run <- filtRs[meta_2run$Unique_ID]
errR_2run <- learnErrors(filtRs_2run, multithread = TRUE)

# Coral tissue, V2 (65 samples)
filtRs_3run <- filtRs[meta_3run$Unique_ID]
errR_3run <- learnErrors(filtRs_3run, multithread = TRUE)

# Mucus, Y2 (98 samples)
filtRs_4run <- filtRs[meta_4run$Unique_ID]
errR_4run <- learnErrors(filtRs_4run, multithread = TRUE)

# Water, Y2 (21 samples)
filtRs_5run <- filtRs[meta_5run$Unique_ID]
errR_5run <- learnErrors(filtRs_5run, multithread = TRUE)

# Mucus, Z2 (15)
# Need to do this one differently, because it is MiSeq i100 that uses binned quality scores. 
filtRs_6run <- filtRs[meta_6run$Unique_ID]
binnedQs <- c(2, 12, 24, 38)
binnedQualErrfun <- makeBinnedQualErrfun(binnedQs)
errR_6run <-learnErrors(filtRs_6run, errorEstimationFunction=binnedQualErrfun, multi=TRUE)


#Save
save(errR_1run, file = "errR_1run.RData")
save(errR_2run, file = "errR_2run.RData")
save(errR_3run, file = "errR_3run.RData")
```

#Sample Inference
- We are now ready to apply the core sample inference algorithm to the filtered and trimmed sequence data.
- see: https://www.nature.com/articles/nmeth.3869#methods
```{r}
# Coral tissue, R2 (57 samples) 
dadaFs_1run <- dada(filtFs_1run, err=errF_1run, multithread=TRUE)
dadaRs_1run <- dada(filtRs_1run, err=errR_1run, multithread=TRUE)
dadaFs_1run[[12]]

# Water, T2 (26 samples)
dadaFs_2run <- dada(filtFs_2run, err=errF_2run, multithread=TRUE)
dadaRs_2run <- dada(filtRs_2run, err=errR_2run, multithread=TRUE)
dadaFs_2run[[12]]

# Coral tissue, V2 (65 samples)
dadaFs_3run <- dada(filtFs_3run, err=errF_3run, multithread=TRUE)
dadaRs_3run <- dada(filtRs_3run, err=errR_3run, multithread=TRUE)
dadaFs_3run[[12]]

# Mucus, Y2 (98 samples)
dadaFs_4run <- dada(filtFs_4run, err=errF_4run, multithread=TRUE)
dadaRs_4run <- dada(filtRs_4run, err=errR_4run, multithread=TRUE)
dadaFs_4run[[12]]

# Water, Y2 (21 samples)
dadaFs_5run <- dada(filtFs_5run, err=errF_5run, multithread=TRUE)
dadaRs_5run <- dada(filtRs_5run, err=errR_5run, multithread=TRUE)
dadaFs_5run[[12]]

# Mucus, Z2 (15)
dadaFs_6run <- dada(filtFs_6run, err=errF_6run, multithread=TRUE)
dadaRs_6run <- dada(filtRs_6run, err=errR_6run, multithread=TRUE)
dadaFs_6run[[12]]
```

```{r}
head(mergers_1run[[1]])

head(mergers_2run[[1]])

# Inspect the merger data.frame from the first sample

# Inspect the merger data.frame from the first sample
head(mergers_4run[[1]])

# Water, Y2 (21 samples)
mergers_5run <- mergePairs(dadaFs_5run, filtFs_5run, dadaRs_5run, filtRs_5run, verbose=TRUE)
  # Inspect the merger data.frame from the first sample
head(mergers_5run[[1]])

head(mergers_6run[[1]])
```

__________________________________
#Construct sequence table
- We can now construct an amplicon sequence variant table (ASV) table, a higher-resolution version of the OTU table produced by traditional methods.
```{r}
seqtab_1run <- makeSequenceTable(mergers_1run)
dim(seqtab_1run)

seqtab_2run <- makeSequenceTable(mergers_2run)
dim(seqtab_2run)

seqtab_3run <- makeSequenceTable(mergers_3run)
dim(seqtab_3run)

seqtab_4run <- makeSequenceTable(mergers_4run)
dim(seqtab_4run)

seqtab_5run <- makeSequenceTable(mergers_5run)
dim(seqtab_5run)

seqtab_6run <- makeSequenceTable(mergers_6run)
dim(seqtab_6run)

seqtab_all <- mergeSequenceTables(seqtab_1run, seqtab_2run, seqtab_3run, seqtab_4run,  seqtab_5run,  seqtab_6run)                   
```

Inspect distribution of sequence lengths:
Top row of output is the size of the sequence (we want 253), bottom row is how many of each length we have. 
```{r}
table(nchar(getSequences(seqtab_all)))
seqtab2_all <- seqtab_all[,nchar(colnames(seqtab_all)) %in% 252:254]
```



__________________________________
#Remove chimeras
```{r}

seqtab_all.nochim <- removeBimeraDenovo(seqtab2_all, method="consensus", multithread=2, verbose=TRUE)
dim(seqtab_all.nochim)
sum(seqtab_all.nochim)/sum(seqtab_all)


seqtab_final <- seqtab_all.nochim

#Save
save(seqtab_final, file = "seqtab_final.RData")
```




__________________________________
#Track reads through the pipeline
- As a final check of our progress, we’ll look at the number of reads that made it through each step in the pipeline:
```{r}
getN <- function(x) sum(getUniques(x))

dadaFs_all <- c(dadaFs_1run, dadaFs_2run, dadaFs_3run, dadaFs_4run, dadaFs_5run, dadaFs_6run)
dadaRs_all <- c(dadaRs_1run, dadaRs_2run, dadaRs_3run, dadaRs_4run, dadaRs_5run, dadaRs_6run)
merger_all <- c(mergers_1run, mergers_2run, mergers_3run, mergers_4run, mergers_5run, mergers_6run)

track <- cbind(out, sapply(dadaFs_all, getN), sapply(dadaRs_all, getN), sapply(merger_all, getN), rowSums(seqtab_final))
colnames(track) <- c("input", "filtered", "denoisedF", "denoisedR", "merged", "nonchim")
rownames(track) <- sample.names 
head(track)

#look at percentages
track.df <- as.data.frame(track)

track.df$dF_percent <- track.df$denoisedF/track.df$filtered
track.df$dR_percent <- track.df$denoisedR/track.df$filtered
track.df$merge_percent <- track.df$merged/track.df$denoisedF
track.df$nochim_percent <- track.df$nonchim/track.df$merged
head(track.df)

#Save
write.csv(track.df, file = "track_through_dada2.csv")
```

Add species
```{r}
# taxa <- addSpecies(taxa, "~/Documents/WHOI/silva_species_assignment_v138.1.fa.gz")
```

addSpecies() keeps on failing and making my R crash, so trying this work around from: https://github.com/benjjneb/dada2/issues/733
```{r}
chunk.size <- 4000
chunks <- split(c(1:nrow(taxa)),
sort(c(1:nrow(taxa))%%ceiling(nrow(taxa)/chunk.size)))

chunks.species <- lapply(chunks,
function(x){
return(addSpecies(taxa[x,],
refFasta = "~/Documents/WHOI/silva_species_assignment_v138.1.fa.gz", verbose = TRUE))
})
taxa.species <- do.call(rbind, chunks.species)


save(taxa.species, file="taxa.RData")
```



```{r}
#Let’s inspect the taxonomic assignments:
taxa.print <- taxa.species 
rownames(taxa.print) <- NULL # Removing sequence rownames for display only
head(taxa.print)
```

Replace the NAs with "unknown"
```{r}
#Replace the NAs with "unknown"
taxa_df <- as.data.frame(taxa.species)
dim(taxa_df) 
taxa_NA_is_Unknown <- taxa_df %>%
  mutate_all(~ ifelse(is.na(.), "unknown", .))
View(taxa_NA_is_Unknown)


save(taxa_NA_is_Unknown, file="taxa_NA_is_Unknown.RData")
```


Replacing NAs with the lowest taxonomic level 
```{r}
#Replacing NAs with the lowest taxonomic level
#replace NAs with the deepest taxonomy available
taxa_NA_is_LowestTax <- taxa_df
taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Kingdom <- as.character(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Kingdom)
king_na <- which(is.na(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Kingdom))
taxa_NA_is_LowestTax[king_na, "Kingdom"] <- 'Unknown'

taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Phylum <- as.character(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Phylum)
phy_na <- which(is.na(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Phylum))
taxa_NA_is_LowestTax[phy_na, "Phylum"] <- taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Kingdom[phy_na] 

taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Class <- as.character(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Class)
cl_na <- which(is.na(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Class))
taxa_NA_is_LowestTax[cl_na, "Class"] <- taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Phylum[cl_na]

taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Order <- as.character(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Order)
ord_na <- which(is.na(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Order))
taxa_NA_is_LowestTax[ord_na, "Order"] <- taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Class[ord_na]

taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Family <- as.character(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Family)
fam_na <- which(is.na(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Family))
taxa_NA_is_LowestTax[fam_na, "Family"] <- taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Order[fam_na]

taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Genus <- as.character(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Genus)
gen_na <- which(is.na(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Genus))
taxa_NA_is_LowestTax[gen_na, "Genus"] <- taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Family[gen_na]

taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Species <- as.character(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Species)
spec_na <- which(is.na(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Species))
taxa_NA_is_LowestTax[spec_na, "Species"] <- taxa_NA_is_LowestTax$Genus[spec_na]

View(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax)

save(taxa_NA_is_LowestTax, file="taxa_NA_is_LowestTax.RData")
```

#Make ASV tables and taxonomy files
Make sure the seqtab_final file with all the ASVs and the taxa are all in the same order. Save the sequences with an ASV# identifier.
```{r}
otus <- seqtab_final
taxonomy <- taxa_NA_is_LowestTax

idx <- match(rownames(taxonomy), colnames(otus))
otus <- otus[,idx]
#Warn if there's a mismatch.
if (any(is.na(idx))) {
  warning("Some taxonomy row names were not found in OTU column names!")
  print(rownames(taxonomy)[is.na(idx)])
}

#save a dataframe with a new ASV identifier and the sequence from the rownames for taxa
ASVseqs <- data.frame("ASV_ID" = paste0("ASV", seq(from = 1, to = ncol(seqtab_final), by = 1)), "sequence" = rownames(taxonomy))


#rename otu and taxa dataframe so they are easier to interpret
colnames(otus) <- ASVseqs$ASV_ID
rownames(taxonomy) <- ASVseqs$ASV_ID
```



#Save final tables
Write these tables so you have them for future data analysis
```{r}
save(otus, file="otus_LCT_AllSamples_final.RData")
write.table(taxonomy, file = "taxonomy_LCT_AllSamples_final.txt", sep = "\t", row.names = TRUE, col.names = TRUE)
write.table(ASVseqs, file = "ASVsequences_LCT_AllSamples_final.txt", sep = "\t", row.names = TRUE, col.names = TRUE)
```
